title: Launch rotor weekmap and operator checklist memo
summary: Compact week-long plan for a progressive 50% -> 100% traffic ramp (the 'rotor') with an operator concierge model. This doc is the working memo for on-call/shift operators, SRE leads, and release owners. Focus: short timeline, fast instrumentation checks, clear escalation ladders, and a tight post-run retro template.
weekmap:
Day 0 (pre-flight): final merge validation, infra smoke, telemetry dashboards deployed, optional dry-run in staging.
Day 1: 10% traffic window (2 hours) — baseline sampling, latency and error gates.
Day 2: 25% traffic window (3 hours) — perf profiling, KV cache hit-rate observations.
Day 3: 50% ramp (4 hours) — canary cohort expanded, begin cost telemetry sampling.
Day 4: 75% ramp (3 hours) — soak period, begin QA-driven scenario tests.
Day 5: Full roll (100%) with 2h guarded window then normal ops.
Post-roll (Day 6): 24–48h monitoring & annotated release notes, schedule retro and incident hunting if anomalies observed.
operator_checklist:
(Pre-shift) Confirm you have access to: release tag, deploy links, pager rotation, and emergency rollback runbook.
1) Pull latest deploy manifest and compare to staging config (git diff).
2) Confirm canary weights and traffic shaping rules are set in the router.
3) Launch telemetry dashboards (latency p50/p95/p99, error_rate, tokens_per_sec, infra_gpu_util).
4) Verify synthetic canary probes are green (chat + embedding samp).
5) Ensure cache warmers have run for hot paths.
6) Announce start in #deploy-ops and tag product+SRE.
7) During window: monitor anomaly channel; check for rising tail latency or model stalls.
8) If latency > gate OR error spike > gate, initiate stepwise rollback (see rollback_plan).
9) If minor regression, pause ramp and open incident stub with triage owner.
10) After window: snapshot dashboards, export logs for the window, and attach to release ticket.
telemetry_gates:
Primary gates (absolute): p95 latency <= 1.4x baseline, error rate <= +0.5% absolute.
Secondary gates (relative): token generation time median increase <= 20%.
Resource gates: GPU util < 85% sustained over 5 minutes for any node, memory OOMs = 0.
Quality gate: automated eval set (promo prompts) match baseline aggregate score within -2% tolerance.
Escalation: if any primary gate fails for 3 consecutive minutes, operator should escalate to SRE lead and pause the rotor.
Notes: thresholds are conservative for this rotor; we can relax in follow-ups if telemetry shows headroom.
rollback_plan:
A. Soft stepback: reduce canary weight to previous stable (e.g., from 50% -> 25%) and observe 15 minutes.
B. If metrics don't recover: cut traffic to 0% for affected model variant and redirect to fallback model (variant v-stable).
C. If fallback fails or traffic routing misbehaves: abort to last known-good deploy (git tag).
D. Emergency: run infra isolation (drain affected nodes) + full redeploy of stable image.
Communications: use /ops-announce with template: "Rollback initiated — reason, step taken, ETA for update". Post-rollback: attach timeline, logs, and initial hypothesis to OPS ticket.
release_notes_draft:
- Feature: Routing policy update to support progressive 'rotor' weighted canaries for model variants. Improves reliability during model swaps.
- Ops: New operator concierge runbook included for 1-week ramp schedules.
- Perf: Kernel selector improvements reduce median token time by ~6% on short contexts (internal measure).
- Known issue: Under rare long-context synthetic loads, p99 latency can spike; we've added a guarded throttle and will roll further mitigations in next patch.
Include: links to telemetry dashboards and troubleshooting checklist in the public release notes section.
open_questions:
- Do we want product to approve the 75% -> 100% step on Day 5 or should SRE auto-advance after 1h soak?
- Should we enable additional logging on the embed path for the 50% window (cost vs value tradeoff)?
- Where to persist the per-shift snapshots? (current plan: attach to Jira OPS-2345 but need retention confirm).
- Make operator rotation: is 2 person overlap enough for night windows? (ask people-ops for preference).
notes_to_self: Keep the first 10 minutes of every window for synthetic probe warmup. If a metric drifts slowly, prefer stepback over full rollback to gather forensic signals. Save all console exports as artifacts named: rotor-<date>-<window>-snap.json. Use 'rotor' as the canonical tag in all comms for searchability.
post_run_template:
1) Window summary (who, when, traffic weights)
2) Metrics snapshot (attach charts)
3) Incidents/alerts fired (list with timelines)
4) Actions taken (ramp, pause, rollback)
5) Quick hypothesis and follow-ups (owner + ETA)
6) Link to artefacts: logs, exported snapshots, and PRs
7) Retro notes: what went well, what we missed, friction items to fix next rotor.
conclusion: This memo is intentionally compact — operationally actionable items up front, investigative artifacts after. Please iterate on thresholds and add product or SRE signoff inline. We'll run a dry-run two days before the scheduled rotor to validate ops flow.
author_notes: Drafted during sprint planning. Expect tweaks after dry-run. If you edit, add initials and date at the bottom of the document to keep a quick audit trail.
